LESSON: LANGUAGE USE 4.3.1 SINGULAR AND PLURALS (ADD -S AND - ES)

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade one
Subject: General
Strand: Strand 4
Topic 4.3: Language Use 4.3.1 Singular and plurals (add -s and - es)
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Language Use 4.3.1 Singular and plurals (add -s and - es), part of Strand 4 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade one General.

Key inquiry question: What objects are found at home?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Language Use 4.3.1 Singular and plurals (add -s and - es) together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Digital literacy: The learner creates with technology as they recite and record poems containing singular and plural

Values:
Unity: inclusion is promoted as learners take different roles in group activities.

Pertinent Contemporary Issues :

• Citizenship-social cohesion is enhanced as learners work together in groups cooperatively.

• Life skills (Self-awareness): The learner’s self-esteem is enhanced as they use singular and plural nouns which require an addition –s and –es.

Link to other learning areas:

The learners relate the concept of singular and plural to the concept of counting learnt in mathematics activities.

Suggested Learning Resources

Manual alphabet chart, flash cards, internet, posters, online dictionaries, assistive devices fitted with appropriate technologies such as hearing aids and

amplifiers, adapted course books, flash cards, sign language dictionary, internet, signed audio-visual recordings
